title: Muscular Force
description: The Baron freezes all machines, but your muscles still work! Learn about contact forces to grab shard 2.

content.value: Some forces act only when two objects TOUCH. These are called CONTACT FORCES. The two everyday contact forces are muscular force and friction.

The force our body applies using muscles is called MUSCULAR FORCE. Lifting a bag, pushing a door, and chewing food all use muscular force. Animals use it too — bullocks pull carts, horses pull carriages.
Even actions inside your body use muscular force! Your heart muscles pump blood and the muscles of your food pipe push food down to your stomach — all thanks to muscular force.

MUSCULAR FORCE IN ACTION
🏋️  lifting a weight        🐂  a bullock pulling a cart
🚪  pushing a door          🫀  the heart pumping blood
🍽️  chewing food           💪  an arm bending
Muscular force is always a CONTACT force — your muscles must be in contact (directly or through your body) with the object they move.
Key Takeaway: Contact forces act only when objects touch. Muscular force is the force applied by muscles — used to lift, push, chew, and even pump blood inside the body.

quiz.question: A contact force acts…
options: across empty space with no touching
quiz.explain: Contact forces, like muscular force and friction, require the objects to be in contact.

quiz.question: Which of these uses muscular force?
options: A magnet attracting a nail from a distance
The Earth pulling a falling apple
quiz.explain: A bullock uses its muscles (in contact with the cart via a rope/yoke) — that's muscular force. The other two are non-contact forces.

quiz.question: Your heart pumping blood is an example of…
quiz.explain: Heart muscles apply muscular force to pump blood — muscular force works inside the body too.
